decisionRules.name: validity
decisionRules.text: An arm-rep is INVALID, re-queued and never averaged, if any of these hold: `idle` < 60 s in any boxwatch sample; `gpu3d_other` > 5%; any non-test process using >= 1 CPU core-equivalent in any sample [D threshold; the bench-1 Seagate Toolkit case]; entity count differs from arm A by > 10% (R3-0 server-state pin) [D threshold]; console errors > 0; dev wasm; wrong adapter. If two scheduled windows yield no valid reps for an arm, accept 5 reps with a reported A/A noise in place of the idle gate, and mark the result "noisy box".
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py rule_v / assess (`--noisy-box` for the fallback); the >= 1 core test reads >= 0.95 core-equivalents over the ~2 s sample window; a rep overlapping a boxEvents cpu-hog entry is CONTAMINATED; a rep with no box sample at all is INVALID (unverified). hbbench items: `hbreport.py bench ... --queue <this file>` (each gated arm held to its gate). hbanatomy --eval items: scripts/perf-worker/s1_eval_report.py, which calls the same hbreport.assess with this file's gates and boxEvents.

decisionRules.name: noise
decisionRules.text: noise = max(|A - A'|, half of A's rep spread). A delta is real only if it exceeds max(2 x noise, 3% fps or 0.5 ms).
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py noise_of / compare (frame-count metrics use a floor of 1); scripts/perf-worker/s1_eval_report.py calls the same compare on the eval windows.

decisionRules.name: scoring
decisionRules.text: Score on the binding thread's ms (main busy per frame, CrGpuMain WEBGL per present, GPU ms), plus still / moving / tour fps, p50 / p95, h100 / h250 / max / jank. Never on draw counts alone; draw counts are heading-binned and reported with multidraw ranges.

decisionRules.name: keep
decisionRules.text: A perf change goes or stays default-on only if all five hold: (i) its binding-thread ms moved by >= 50% of the prediction; (ii) at least one of still / moving / tour fps improved by a real delta, and no segment regressed by one; (iii) hitch metrics not worse by a real delta; (iv) 0 console errors; (v) the look gate (R4) passed. Otherwise it goes off and keeps its code only if a later step needs it. INCONCLUSIVE gets 3 more reps once, then goes off. For a hitch change (R3-2's upload draw and worker-wait fixes, scored on hitch metrics per R3-2), (i) and (ii) read on its predicted hitch metrics instead: first-turn max and h100 better by a real delta, and no still / moving / tour fps segment worse by one.
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py r3_keep (predictions from each arm's `predict`; look gate from `--look ARM=pass|fail`; binding-thread ms from hbanatomy runs of both arms). Hitch changes (UWD-on / R-UWD, BFW-on / R-BFW) read (i) and (ii) on first-turn max and h100 per this rule's last sentence (re-copied 2026-10-30 by lane Q2; it settles the hitch-flag point lane Q had left OPEN for the owner). hbreport r3_keep has no hitch reading yet: for those arms its printed R3 verdict is not the verdict, and each arm's decisionRule says which compare rows decide.

decisionRules.name: look
decisionRules.text: WHAT kernels: bit-exact, or <= 1 f32 ulp, in node or cargo; array layers byte-equal on the 1070 readback. HOW changes: rc-eye stills at 1080p with `skytime=13`, compared by `rc_eye_diff.py`, with particles and sway masked. Default threshold: <= 1% of pixels over 8/255 and <= 0.1% over 32/255; each step may set a tighter one. Every heatmap gets a structural review. Then the batched owner eye test; the owner can veto.

decisionRules.name: routing
decisionRules.text: The binding thread is the largest of main busy per frame, CrGpuMain per present, and GPU ms, at the tier's resolution. If GPU ms >= 0.9 x frame time, GPU levers go first. If CrGpuMain >= main, GL-command levers go first (batching, HUD raster). Otherwise main-thread levers. Never claim fps for a lever on a thread that is not binding; book its ms as headroom.

decisionRules.name: stop
decisionRules.text: A structural lane that delivers < 50% of its predicted ms at stage A stops before stage B and gets a written post-mortem.
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py r6_stop (applies to entityBatch, PENDING here).

decisionRules.name: tier presets
decisionRules.text: A tier preset change ships only if it moves the over-budget thread under its ceiling, or is look-neutral and cheaper. Ultra looks change only with explicit owner OK. This includes `objRadius` and any governor knob.

decisionRules.name: probe gate
decisionRules.text: If the M1 structure-ceiling probe's V1/V2 do not cut main-thread world-render ms and CrGpuMain WEBGL ms by >= 40% against V0 on the 1070, R3-4 and R3-5 are re-scoped before any L-sized build: smaller stage A, or GPU-side levers first under R5.
decisionRules.implementation: M1a-CEILING (batch-R3-M1); gates the PENDING entityBatch build, not an S1 arm.

decisionRules.name: WebGPU
decisionRules.text: Go only on the R3-12 criteria plus the owner's charter amendment.

decisionRules.name: reference clients
decisionRules.text: WebAC, OpenAC and upstream numbers are bounds that say which half of the frame to attack. They are never targets, never a pass/fail gate for a step, and never mixed into B0 comparisons. A reference reading on a different machine or content is quoted with that machine and content.

west4.what: Four westward one-landblock @teleloc hops from the Holtburg bench point, then the return to it (lanes R / R2 / W2: 'westward @teleloc hops with a turn after each'). Holtburg's 11x11 residency ring keeps the next landblock's terrain resident, so each hop streams one new column of objects / cells / anim scenery at the ring edge plus the hop target's detail.
west4.derivation: Ground z = the retail terrain height under the stop: the LandBlock heights of ~/ac_base_dats/client_cell_1.dat (0xXXYYFFFF) through the LandHeightTable of Region 0x13000000 (client_portal.dat), sampled on the client's split triangle (WorldBuilder.Shared TerrainAlgorithms.SampleHeightTriangle / IsSWtoNEcut), parsed with WorldBuilder.Terminal chorizite-parse-dat-record (lane Q2 scratch terrain_h.py). The sampler reproduces every groundSamples z below (generated-scenery placements of the base-DAT bake, whose z is the terrain height) to 0.01 m. Well grounded = groundZ known, no DAT building or static (LandBlockInfo 0xXXYYFFFE) within 9 m of the stop (nearestDatObjectM) and the requested z between groundZ and groundZ + 7 m (expectedDropM), so the player falls at most 7 m onto the terrain: ACE deals falling damage only beyond ~15.75 m/s of fall (Player_Move.cs HandleFallingDamage: 11.25 + 4.5), i.e. ~12.7 m. Each stop is near the landblock centre and >= 70 m from every hostile spawn of the bake's spawn layer in its own and the 8 neighbouring landblocks (creatures other than Harmless generators, chickens and rabbits; w1 107 m, w2 72 m, w3 87 m, w4 80 m). Outdoor cell = floor(x/24)*8 + floor(y/24) + 1. 0xA4B4 has no point >= 70 m from its hostile spawns (best 62 m: Gnawer Shreth / Shrethlet, Mite Snippet, Hollow Minion, Newbie Aluvian generators), so the route turns home after 0xA5B4 (4 hops + the return, not 5).

landing.rule: ONE landing rule for every check in this file (S1-PRE laptop tab check, S1-ROUTE, S1-DIAG; s1.eval.js landing()): the player stands on the retail terrain under the stop, |stand z - groundZ| <= tolM (not under the ground, not on a roof or a tree). Then dropM = z - stand z lies within expectedDropM +- tolM (-1 ... 7.37 m over this route, under ACE's ~12.7 m fall-damage threshold). A failed landing is a result.problems entry (route.notLanded counts them).

items.title: WEBGL_lose_context loseContext(), await the lost event + a frame (fast) or + 500 ms (slow), restoreContext(), await the restored event, 20 s of per-frame batch status; 1 rep each
items.segments: hbanatomy --eval boot at Holtburg (the gate needs an ACTIVE batch), then s1.eval.js ctxloss: take the WEBGL_lose_context handle while the context is alive; loseContext(); await 'webglcontextlost'; await a frame (fast) or 500 ms + a frame (slow); drain getError (CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL expected); restoreContext(); drain getError (INVALID_OPERATION = refused); await 'webglcontextrestored'; 20 s of per-frame batch status; drain getError at the end
items.note: Chrome dispatches 'webglcontextlost' in a queued task and allows restoreContext() only after that event was dispatched with its default prevented (three and webgl_context_recovery.js prevent it; restore_allowed is set when the dispatch returns), so a restore in the SAME task as loseContext() (the K2 handoff's 'back-to-back', corrected by verifier K2), in the lost listener or in a microtask after it, is refused with INVALID_OPERATION and the canvas stays lost. s1.eval.js therefore restores one frame after the event (fast) or 500 ms after it (slow), reads the refusal back from getError, and awaits 'webglcontextrestored' before the watch. The app pauses its frame pump while lost (webgl_context_recovery.js onPause) and resumes at 'restored' (or after re-hydrating released textures); the K2 canvas listener tears the batches down at both events, so legacy buckets show until the re-plan. tests/s1_queue.test.mjs drives both modes against a fake GL with these semantics, and a back-to-back restore against it reads as refused.
